text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek was named the political personality of the month in an opinion poll.
- Railway unions said they would continue their strike, which ended on Saturday, next Thursday, if their demands for higher salaries are not met by then.
- Health resort Terme Catez said the number of visitors in April and May was higher than in the same period last year.
- Breda Pecan, a member of the leftist United List of Social Democrats, was elected mayor of the seaside town of Izola on Sunday.

- If elections were held this week, nearly 30 percent of Slovenians would support the centre-left Liberal Democrats while the conservative People's Party would come second with 11 percent of votes, an opinion poll showed.
- The Green Party of Slovenia, which did not make it to parliament in November elections, is deeply divided after two camps elected two different presidents on Friday.
- The border crossing Dolga vas between Slovenia and Hungary still needs to be improved on the Slovenian side to accelerate traffic flow between the two countries.
